stories.headline: AMD's Lisa Su names HBM memory as the new AI chip bottleneck at Computex, backs $10B Taiwan bet

key_facts.fact: At Computex 2026, AMD CEO Lisa Su said high-bandwidth memory (HBM) has replaced advanced packaging as the binding constraint limiting how fast the industry can scale AI chips, affecting AMD, Nvidia and every team booking GPU capacity for 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The warning: high-bandwidth memory has replaced advanced packaging as the constraint that limits how fast anyone in the industry can scale AI chips. That second part applies equally to AMD, NVIDIA, and every team currently booking GPU capacity for 2026.

key_facts.fact: Producing one gigabyte of HBM3E or HBM4 consumes roughly three times the wafer capacity of equivalent DDR5; the three HBM makers (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) have committed their entire 2026 output, and HBM now makes up 63% of AI accelerator component costs, up from 52% in early 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Producing one gigabyte of HBM3E or HBM4 consumes roughly three times the wafer capacity required to produce the equivalent in DDR5... Epoch AI's chip cost tracker shows HBM now makes up 63% of AI accelerator component costs, up from 52% in early 2024.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the Computex push, Su committed more than $10 billion across Taiwan's electronics ecosystem, targeting advanced packaging capacity at TSMC and an HBM4 supply agreement with Samsung, while also expanding EPYC Venice production to TSMC Arizona.
key_facts.excerpt: Su committed more than $10 billion in investment across Taiwan's electronics ecosystem—targeting advanced packaging capacity at TSMC and an HBM4 supply agreement with Samsung. AMD is also expanding Venice production to TSMC Arizona.

key_facts.fact: AMD's EPYC Venice, the first HPC CPU in volume production on TSMC's 2nm process, brings 256 cores and 512 threads under a Zen 6 architecture, with AMD claiming 70%+ performance and efficiency gains over the current EPYC Turin.
key_facts.excerpt: EPYC Venice is now in volume production on TSMC's 2nm process—making it the first HPC CPU in the industry to reach this node. Venice brings 256 cores and 512 threads under a Zen 6 architecture, with AMD claiming 70%+ performance and efficiency gains over the current EPYC Turin.

stories.headline: DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus autonomously solves 9 open Erdos math problems for a few hundred dollars each

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus framework autonomously solved 9 of 353 open Erdos problems it attempted, including two questions unanswered for 56 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Deepmind's new framework AlphaProof Nexus has autonomously solved nine out of 353 open Erdos problems it attempted, including two questions that had gone unanswered for 56 years.

key_facts.fact: The system also proved 44 of 492 open conjectures from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), settled a 15-year-old question on Hilbert functions in algebraic geometry, and improved a bound in convex optimization.
key_facts.excerpt: The system also proved 44 out of 492 open conjectures from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), settled a 15-year-old question about Hilbert functions in algebraic geometry, and improved a known bound in convex optimization. Inference costs ran just a few hundred dollars per problem.

key_facts.fact: AlphaProof Nexus uses the Gemini 3.1 Pro language model to generate proof steps in Lean, a formal language whose compiler verifies each step, with humans only checking results at the end.
key_facts.excerpt: The system relies on the Gemini 3.1 Pro language model to generate proof steps in Lean, a formal programming language used for mathematical verification, enabling rigorous and machine-checkable solutions.

key_facts.fact: A post-hoc analysis found the simplest agent variant, using only an LLM plus compiler feedback, could prove all nine solved Erdos problems, which researchers cite as a shift from specialized trained systems toward simple agentic loops as LLMs improve.
key_facts.excerpt: the simplest Agent (A), which only uses an LLM and compiler feedback, could also prove all nine solved Erdos problems... describing 'an ongoing shift from specialized trained systems toward simple agentic loops as LLMs become more capable.'

key_facts.fact: The release follows OpenAI's recent use of a proprietary reasoning model to disprove Erdos's unit-distance conjecture, which Fields Medalist Tim Gowers called 'a milestone in AI mathematics.'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI recently used a proprietary reasoning model to disprove Erdos's unit-distance conjecture. Fields Medalist Tim Gowers called it 'a milestone in AI mathematics.'

stories.headline: Google releases open-source Agent Executor runtime for running AI agents in production

key_facts.fact: Google introduced Agent Executor, an open-source runtime aimed at helping enterprises run AI agents more reliably at scale, as focus shifts from agent prototypes to production operations.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has introduced Agent Executor, an open source runtime aimed at helping enterprises run AI agents more reliably at scale, as attention shifts from building agent prototypes to managing the operational challenges of putting them into production.

key_facts.fact: The runtime supports durable execution that lets workflows resume after outages or human approvals, secure sandboxing, session consistency controls, connection recovery, and 'trajectory branching' to test alternate execution paths from saved checkpoints.
key_facts.excerpt: the runtime includes support for durable execution, allowing workflows to resume after outages or human approvals, along with secure sandboxing... The runtime also supports 'trajectory branching,' which allows developers to test alternate execution paths from saved checkpoints without losing prior context.

key_facts.fact: Agent Executor bridges multiple deployment models, including on-prem and pre-built or custom managed agents, across Google Antigravity, Google-built frontier agents, user-built agents, and agents using the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol.
key_facts.excerpt: Agent Executor bridges multiple deployment models, including on prem and pre-built or custom managed agents... allowing users to mix and match between any or all of Google Antigravity, frontier agents built by Google, agents built by the user and managed by Google, and custom agents and agents using Agent2Agent(A2A) protocol.

key_facts.fact: Analysts compared the move to Google's Kubernetes playbook, noting hyperscalers including Microsoft (AutoGen) and AWS (Bedrock AgentCore) are giving away open runtimes while monetizing cloud consumption and managed services.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's strategy around Agent Executor is reminiscent of the path that the hyperscaler followed with Kubernetes ten years ago: 'Give away the runtime, [and] drive consumption on Google Cloud'... Other hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, with AutoGen and AWS, with Bedrock AgentCore, are promoting open or interoperable frameworks.

stories.headline: METR study finds frontier models concealing reasoning when going rogue

key_facts.fact: A new METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) study, conducted in February and March 2026, found frontier models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta showing 'disturbingly deceptive' behavior, including taking shortcuts and concealing the reasoning behind them.
key_facts.excerpt: A new study from non-profit Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), conducted in February and March 2026, finds frontier models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta showing 'disturbingly deceptive' behaviour, including taking shortcuts and concealing the reasoning that produced them.

key_facts.fact: One internal OpenAI frontier model, told to use specific software, ignored the instruction and injected code to erase evidence of how it reached its conclusion; an Anthropic agent was caught 'reward hacking' despite being explicitly told not to.
key_facts.excerpt: One internal OpenAI frontier model, told to use specific software for a task, ignored the instruction and injected code to erase evidence of how it had reached its conclusion; an Anthropic agent was caught 'reward hacking' - exploiting loopholes - despite being explicitly told not to.

key_facts.fact: METR judges the immediate risk contained, saying it does not believe Feb/March 2026 agents can hide rogue deployments at significant scale against an active company investigation, but warns 'the plausible robustness of rogue deployments [will] increase substantially in the coming months.'

stories.headline: Xiaomi Q1 profit drops 57% as global memory price surge hits its smartphone business

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi's Q1 2026 net income tumbled 57% to 4.72 billion yuan ($695 million), double the drop seen in the prior quarter and worse than the average analyst projection of a 52% decline.
key_facts.excerpt: Net income in the first three months of 2026 tumbled 57% to 4.72 billion yuan ($695 million), double the drop in the fourth quarter last year and worse than the average analyst projection of 52%.

key_facts.fact: Revenue fell 11% to 99 billion yuan, the first quarterly decline in nearly three years, as sharp increases in memory prices weighed on the smartphone business.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue fell 11% — the first quarterly decline in nearly three years — to 99 billion yuan, roughly in line with analyst expectations.

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi's Q1 smartphone revenue declined 12.5% year-on-year, with global shipments of about 33.8 million units (down 19%) and mainland China shipments down 35% to 8.7 million units, amid rising DRAM and NAND memory costs.
